content_sections.title: A routine and a past action
content_sections.body_text: Read: ‘I run home every Friday.’ This happens again and again. Read: ‘I ran home yesterday.’ This happened before today and is over. Run changes to ran. Write the two lines from memory, then check run + every Friday and ran + yesterday.

content_sections.title: Why did Mai run?
content_sections.body_text: Mai was late, so she ran to the station. Run here means move on foot faster than walking. Read: ‘Mai ran to the station because she was late.’ Change station to gate or home. Keep ran and a past time.

content_sections.title: Ask for useful help
content_sections.body_text: Mai: ‘I ran to the station because I was late. Now I cannot find Gate 2. Please help me.’ Ben: ‘Yes. Gate 2 is beside the café.’ Mai: ‘Thank you.’ Read both roles. The reply solves Mai’s problem. Change only the gate number and place.

content_sections.title: Clap, write, listen, speak
content_sections.body_text: Clap ran once, sta-tion twice, and yes-ter-day three times. Write the dialogue from memory and compare it with the model. Record it, hide the text, replay, and write two things you hear: why Mai ran and what help she needs. Uncover the model to check. Then say both roles again without reading.
